USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the October 10–11 Washington round to test a limited, enforceable truce without adding new tariffs or giving up existing ones. Keep List 3 at 25%, List 4A at 15%, Huawei on the Entity List, and the December 15 List 4B threat as leverage, but do not implement the scheduled October 15 hike from 25% to 30% while Liu He is at the table unless China walks away. Seek a written, time-bound package of farm and energy purchases plus a freeze on further tit-for-tat; do not trade away structural IP/enforcement language for a photo-op, and do not offer a partial or full rollback until Beijing puts matching, verifiable commitments on paper.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not existential. The dispute has already raised List 3 to 25% (2019-05-10), put Huawei on the Entity List (2019-05-16), designated China a currency manipulator after CNY broke 7 (2019-08-05), and put 15% duties on List 4A (~$110–125B) from September 1, with China answering on ~$75B including autos. US farm exports to China remain the exposed sector: monthly goods exports to China are only ~$8.9B versus ~$39.8B of imports, and reporting through July showed ag/food shipments down more than 50% year-on-year, with soybeans accounting for most of the drop. Markets are pricing stress rather than boom: the 10-year yield is 1.59% (down ~96 bp in the lookback), the 2-year is 1.47%, VIX is 18.64 after an August spike to 24.59, Michigan sentiment fell from 100 to 89.8 in August before recovering only to 95.5, and industrial production is slightly softer. A stronger dollar and CNY near 7.13 also blunt tariff incidence. That is material drag and political heat in the farm belt—not a recessionary tariff cascade or a lost tech position.

The same evidence argues against both further escalation this week and unearned concession. China is already signaling goodwill that can be banked in talks: September tariff-exemption lists, state-media farm exclusions, soybean/pork waivers (roughly 5–6 million tonnes reported) and a rebound in US soybean sales into China ahead of this round. Trump already delayed the 25%→30% step from October 1 to October 15 as a gesture around the PRC anniversary, precisely so this meeting could happen first. Escalating on October 15 while Liu He is in Washington would likely produce a walkout and another farm/auto retaliatory tranche. Full or partial rollback, or large new US purchase/structural giveaways, would be premature: Chinese officials have narrowed the offer and are described as unwilling to lock in industrial-policy or subsidy reform, Liu is not traveling as Xi’s “special envoy,” and the May collapse followed a last-minute text walk-back. Negotiate, keep current tariffs as the walk-away, and treat October 15 and December 15 as contingent—not as today’s move.
key_factors: 13th-round Liu He–Lighthizer/Mnuchin talks in Washington on Oct 10–11 with low Chinese expectations and a narrowed offer
Scheduled Oct 15 hike of existing 25% duties on ~$250B to 30%, already delayed from Oct 1 as a goodwill gesture
Dec 15 List 4B still hanging over phones, laptops, toys and apparel (holiday consumer incidence)
China soybean/pork waivers and renewed cargoes as a reversible goodwill signal, not a structural settlement
US farm-belt exposure and collapsed ag exports versus still-large US imports from China
Market and macro stress (yield collapse, VIX, August sentiment drop) without a US recession print
CNY above 7 and a firmer dollar offsetting some tariff leverage
Huawei Entity List / Meng-Kovrig-Spavor track still open and not suitable as a cheap concession
Hong Kong overlay raising the political temperature of the same week’s talks

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator.
USTR splits List 4: List 4A effective Sept 1; List 4B (cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel) delayed to Dec 15.
China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods including re-imposing tariffs on US autos; Trump directs a 5-point increase on List 4.
List 4A takes effect at 15%; China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs.
US 10-year yield 1.59% on 2019-10-09, down ~96 bp over the window.
Michigan sentiment fell to 89.8 in August, recovered only to 95.5 by October.
US goods exports to China ~$8.85B in the latest month versus ~$39.8B of imports (IMPCH).
CNY at 7.1316 per USD on 2019-10-09 after breaking 7 in early August.
VIX 18.64 on 2019-10-09 after an August 5 spike to 24.59.
Trump delayed the 25% to 30% hike on $250B of Chinese goods from October 1 to October 15 as a gesture of goodwill at Liu He's request around the PRC 70th anniversary.
13th-round talks Oct 10–11; Liu He not traveling as Xi special envoy; Chinese side toning down expectations and may shorten the Washington stay.
China issued more soybean tariff waivers and bought additional cargoes; officials signaled a narrowed offer that would not include industrial-policy or subsidy reform.
